Subject: Proposal: short-term overprovisioning credit + uptier path

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning. To recap, EdgeFin is expecting a brief but material traffic spike for the Dec 10 product rollout. We discussed a short-window headroom option rather than a longer-term commit change.

Attached is a 2-page temp headroom quote (edgefin_temp_headroom_quote.pdf) and an illustrative pricing matrix (uptier_pricing_matrix.xlsx). Key points:
- Temporary overprovisioning window: 14 days starting on request activation.
- Credit structure: pro-rated credit applied to overrun tokens (applies only to pay-as-you-go overages during the window).
- Uptier roadmap: if sustained usage beyond the window, we recommend a phased uptier (30/60/90 day checkpoints) to move to a reserved capacity package with blended rate.

Ask: can you confirm whether procurement needs a PO before we activate the headroom window, or whether DocuSign SOW + internal PO within 10 business days is acceptable? If you can send procurement contact info I’ll route the legal amendment.

Next step: if procurement is OK with the DocuSign -> PO flow, I can ship a signed SOW and enable the window same day we receive the signed DocuSign.

Cheers,

Mina, thanks for the clear summary and materials. A few quick clarifications from procurement and finance:

1) Credit math: how exactly will the pro-rated credit apply? Is it a percentage of overrun spend during the window or a capped USD credit? We need the exact calculation to map to our internal billing system.

2) PO timing: procurement prefers a PO up front for any invoiceable piece, but we can accept a signed DocuSign SOW and follow with PO within 7-10 business days if the SOW includes the temporary credit language and a clear invoice schedule.

3) Legal: can Redwood accept an amendment (one-page) to the existing MSA that defines the headroom window / credit and explicitly states that any longer uptier will be handled via a separate SOW? That keeps legal review light.

If you can provide a one-paragraph credit definition and draft amendment, we’ll fast-track. I’m in a tight loop this week but can approve if legal is minimal.

—Samir

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Proposal: short-term overprovisioning credit + uptier path

Folks — forwarding Samir's questions (below). Procurement at EdgeFin will accept DocuSign + PO within 7-10 business days but needs an explicit credit definition and a one-page amendment to avoid a long legal cycle.

Proposed recommendation (for legal & finance):
- Credit definition: Redwood will apply a USD credit equal to 20% of the net overrun spend incurred by EdgeFin during the active headroom window. The credit will appear on the next invoice following the window and can be applied against the first invoice after the window (not refundable). Example line to include in amendment: "For the duration of the Temporary Headroom Window, Redwood will apply a one-time credit equal to 20% of charges billed for overrun usage incurred during the Window. The credit will be applied to the invoice immediately following the Window; any remaining balance will be billed per the standard invoice cadence."
- Cap: suggest a $75k cap on the credit for this event to limit exposure.
- Activation: DocuSign SOW signature triggers activation; procurement to issue PO within 7-10 business days.
- Uptier path: include 30/60/90 usage checkpoints and a simple statement that any sustained uplift will move to a reserved-capacity SOW with a 30-day notice.

Ben — need a quick sanity check on the 20% credit + $75k cap (numbers are conservative relative to quote). Laura — can you pre-approve a one-page amendment and mark legal priority as low-touch? Jordan — if we accept, I’ll prepare the DocuSign envelope and the short amendment for signature.

Thanks,
Mina
